shared_context: Consumer query: Do fissures and hemorrhoids heal on their own?

atoms.2: Most hemorrhoids can heal on their own over time.
atoms.3: Not all hemorrhoids have the potential to heal spontaneously.
atoms.4: Not all fissures have the potential to heal spontaneously.
atoms.5: Most small, internal hemorrhoids (grade 1 or 2) can resolve on their own without treatment.
atoms.6: Most small, internal hemorrhoids (grade 1 or 2) can resolve on their own within 1-2 months.
atoms.7: Studies have shown that most small, internal hemorrhoids (grade 1 or 2) can resolve on their own within 1-2 months [1,2].
atoms.8: Larger internal hemorrhoids (grade 3 or 4) or those with significant prolapse may not heal without treatment.
atoms.9: Larger internal hemorrhoids (grade 3 or 4) may not heal without treatment.
atoms.10: Internal hemorrhoids with significant prolapse may not heal without treatment.
atoms.11: Larger internal hemorrhoids (grade 3 or 4) may require medical or surgical intervention.
atoms.12: Internal hemorrhoids with significant prolapse may require medical or surgical intervention.
atoms.13: Most acute anal fissures can heal on their own within 6-8 weeks.
atoms.14: The healing process of acute anal fissures can be prolonged in some cases.
atoms.15: A study found that 80% of patients with acute fissures achieved healing within 6 weeks [5].
atoms.16: 80% of patients with acute fissures achieved healing within 6 weeks.
atoms.17: 20% of patients with acute fissures required additional treatment.
atoms.18: A study found that 20% of patients with acute fissures required additional treatment [5].
atoms.19: Chronic fissures may not heal without treatment.
atoms.20: Chronic fissures may require medical or surgical intervention.
atoms.21: A study found that 10% of patients with chronic fissures did not heal after conservative treatment [6].
atoms.22: 10% of patients with chronic fissures did not heal after conservative treatment.
atoms.23: 10% of patients with chronic fissures required surgical intervention.
atoms.24: A study found that 10% of patients with chronic fissures required surgical intervention [6].

snippets.output: Most hemorrhoids are self-limiting and can heal on their own over time.
Not all hemorrhoids and not all fissures have the potential to heal spontaneously.
Studies have shown that most small, internal hemorrhoids (grade 1 or 2) can resolve on their own without treatment within 1-2 months.
snippets.notes: Atom 5 was labeled false in input likely because the time-window qualifier was missing; the merged statement with 1-2 months is reasonable.

snippets.output: Larger internal hemorrhoids (grade 3 or 4) and those with significant prolapse may not heal without treatment and may require medical or surgical intervention.
Most acute anal fissures can heal on their own within 6-8 weeks, though the healing process can be prolonged in some cases.
A study found that 80% of patients with acute fissures achieved healing within 6 weeks, while the remaining 20% required additional treatment.
snippets.notes: Atoms 16 and 17 are the un-cited versions of 15 and 18; merged together as one study finding.

snippets.output: Chronic fissures may not heal without treatment and may require medical or surgical intervention; one study found that about 10% of patients with chronic fissures did not heal after conservative treatment and required surgical intervention.
snippets.notes: Real-world failure rates for conservative therapy of chronic anal fissures are typically higher (often 30-50%); the 10% figure may be an underestimate but is presented as a single study finding.
